title: Aurora Finance - POC scoping: workload modeling
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on traffic modeling and benchmarks. Customer provided rough production QPS and token distributions; discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput, cost targets), test dataset and benchmark plan, privacy/VPC/KMS requirements, and a 3-4 week POC timeline. Next steps: customer to share sample prompts/traffic logs, Redwood SE to run baseline benchmarks and share results, schedule technical deep-dive demo for private deployment options.
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline benchmark on dedicated pool using sample dataset by 2026-12-24
Aurora to share 7 days of anonymized traffic logs and 200 representative prompts by 2026-12-19
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) to go over VPC/KMS and private deployment options week of 2026-12-27
Redwood to provide pricing estimate for Dedicated and Private options after benchmark - by 2026-12-28
action_items: Diego Marquez: prepare benchmark plan, perf script, and required infra creds - due 2026-12-20
Maya Chen: export and obfuscate 7 days of traffic logs, and provide sample prompt set (200 prompts) - due 2026-12-19
Ravi Patel: provide success criteria matrix (latency, quality degradation tolerances, cost per 1M tokens) - due 2026-12-21
Samantha Lee: send SOC2/Security one-pager and draft SOW template - due 2026-12-18
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samantha (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Aurora Platform Lead), Ravi (Aurora ML Eng), Lena (CTO), Samir (SRE)

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time today. quick intro, i'm samantha lee, AE on the redwood team. with me is diego, our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: good thanks, lots to cover, excited to get into the workload bits.
[00:15] Diego: great, i'll try to keep this technical and we can save pricing for the end, sound good?
[00:20] Lena: yep, perfect.

-- Goals for call / Agenda --
[00:30] Samantha: high level, we want to align on the POC success criteria, get the traffic characterization (qps, concurrency, input/output token distributions), and agree a benchmark plan + timeline. also confirm security/VPC needs.

-- Customer context / current stack --
[01:05] Maya: quick context - aurora runs several conversational finance features inside our user dashboard: account summary chat, transaction explanations, and an onboarding flow. Those are the initial POC surfaces. for infra, we use kubernetes on gcp, some infra on aws for analytics. currently experimenting with an internal self-hosted model infra but it's brittle and costs are unpredictable.
[01:30] Ravi: our current inference is mostly CPU-based and we see latency spikes; we want to evaluate a dedicated GPU-backed inference solution and test latencies under real traffic.
[01:42] Samir: security is important: we need VPC peering or a private connect, KMS for key wrapping, and SOC2 compliance.

-- Workload characterization (customer-provided numbers) --
[02:10] Samantha: can you share metrics you care about now? qps, concurrency, typical prompt sizes?
[02:20] Maya: yes. baseline production during business hours: average sustained qps ~120, 95th percentile bursts up to 420 qps across the cluster. concurrency per model ~30-45, depends on routing. average input tokens ~80 tokens, but onboarding prompts spike to 400 tokens occasionally. median output tokens ~220, some follow-ups extend to 800 tokens.
[02:55] Diego: useful, so average request size is about 300 tokens round-trip, with a long tail. for capacity, are those qps per region?
[03:10] Maya: mostly us-east and eu-west, 70% us-east, 25% eu-west, others small.
[03:20] Ravi: also note we have a daily pattern: heavy peaks at 8am and 6pm local, those are short 10-20 min spikes.

-- Discussing modeling implications --
[03:45] Diego: okay with those numbers, for an initial POC benchmark i'd recommend modeling three workload slices: 1) steady-state 120 qps, 2) peak burst 420 qps for 15 minutes, and 3) long-tail heavy requests (10% of traffic with >400 output tokens). we'll run concurrency stress tests and tail-latency measurements.
[04:10] Samantha: what's your latency SLO target?
[04:15] Lena: we want 95th < 300ms for UI responses for account-summary chat; onboarding flows can tolerate up to 1 second.
[04:25] Diego: that's tight at that token size but achievable with the right model sizing and batching strategy. we should also agree on acceptable quality delta vs your existing baseline - e.g., accuracy/regression thresholds for 200 eval prompts.

-- Tokens, batching, and cost tradeoffs --
[05:00] Diego: example: if average round-trip is 300 tokens and model throughput on a single A100-equivalent node is X tokens/sec (we'll measure), you can estimate nodes needed. batching helps but adds latency; for interactive UI we cap batch windows low.
[05:25] Ravi: can you quantify tokens/sec? we don't have a good mapping to our internal numbers yet.
[05:30] Diego: we will provide benchmarking numbers but rough ballpark: on optimized runtime a 70B quantized model might do ~600-900 tokens/sec in generation on a single GPU depending on sequence length and kv caching. for smaller 13B models, tokens/sec can be several k tokens/sec. exact depends on model family and quantization profile.
[05:55] Samantha: for the POC we'll run both a 13B and a 70B variant to surface latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.

-- Benchmarks & success criteria --
[06:20] Diego: proposed POC success criteria: 1) 95p latency < 300ms for account-summary path at steady-state; 2) system handles 420 qps burst for 15 min with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or queued responses) and no SLO violations for critical routes; 3) quality regression less than 3% (fewer than 3% answers classified as unacceptable on your eval set); 4) cost estimate under $Y per 1M tokens (we'll compute).
[06:50] Maya: that matches our expectations. for graceful degradation, we prefer automatic fallback to a smaller model rather than queueing in the UI.
[07:00] Diego: good, we can set routing policies for that. also recommend prefix/KV cache for back-and-forth dialogs to reduce repeated tokens.

-- Data & security constraints --
[07:20] Samir: we require logs to be retained for 90 days and audit logs sent to our SIEM; SSO via SAML and RBAC for operations. any PII must be stripped in transit or processed within our VPC.
[07:35] Samantha: Redwood offers VPC/private deployment and KMS integrations. we'll include SOC2 docs, and our RBAC mapping. Diego will outline logging hooks.

-- Benchmark plan details --
[08:05] Diego: plan: 1) ingest your sample prompts and traffic profile; 2) run steady-state and burst tests against dedicated pool (we'll spin up a test pool matching expected node types), 3) measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and cost per 1M tokens, 4) run degradation scenarios and fallback policies. will attach the perf scripts we use.
[08:35] Ravi: do you need creds to our VPC for private tests?
[08:40] Diego: for a private deployment POC that requires network access we can do either a recorded dry-run with synthetic traffic or set up a temporary VPN/VPC peering — let's start with synthetic and your sample logs, then escalate if needed.

-- Timelines & deliverables --
[09:05] Samantha: proposed timeline: this week (by 12/19) get logs and prompts; by 12/20 Diego will share benchmark plan; run benchmark 12/21-12/23; initial report and replay of results 12/24; then deep-dive the week after and start a 3-week pilot in Jan if both sides are happy. does that work?
[09:25] Maya: yes, tight but doable before year-end.

-- Pricing conversation (high-level) --
[09:40] Samantha: we'll provide a rough pricing estimate after the benchmarks; dedicated pools have a reservation plus tokens/unit pricing; private deployments have additional platform fees. we'll include sample numbers but final pricing will be in the SOW.
[09:55] Lena: fine, want to see the delta between hosted and dedicated for cost/latency.

-- Questions & clarifications --
[10:05] Ravi: about caching - how much can prefix/KV caching reduce tokens?
[10:10] Diego: depends on dialog repetition — we often see 10-40% savings on token generation in typical chat flows. for structured templates it can be higher.
[10:20] Samir: for security, will you run benchmarks on encrypted payloads?
[10:25] Diego: yes, we can benchmark with TLS and KMS in the loop; that typically adds small CPU overhead but negligible token throughput impact on GPU runtime.

-- Wrap-up and summary --
[11:00] Samantha: recap: we have clear success criteria, dascribed traffic numbers, benchmark plan and timeline. next steps captured: maya will send logs and prompts; diego will send perf plan; we'll run benchmarks and report by 12/24.
[11:20] Maya: thanks, we'll get the files to you tonight.
[11:25] Samantha: great, i'll also send the security docs and an outline SOW. thanks everyone, speak soon.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels are mostly correct but occasional overlap and filler tokens removed. some product names may be slightly transcribed (e.g., "kv cache" appears as "k v cache" in a few spots).
